chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat, from Fit'r ibn Khalifa, from Umar ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repels from a group of Muslims an adversity of water or fire, Paradise is obligated for him.'

key_terms.أُوجِبَتْ: Obligated or made obligatory (a technical term indicating a guaranteed reward)
key_terms.عَادِيَة: Adversity or calamity, specifically referring to natural disasters like floods or fire in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for protecting Muslims from water or fire?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the practical dimension of *nasihah* (advising/benefiting) by linking physical protection from elemental hazards like water and fire to the ultimate reward of Paradise. It reflects the Shia emphasis on communal responsibility (*ta'awun*), where safeguarding the community's material well-being is a direct pathway to spiritual salvation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Usna Bin Al Waleed Al hannat Bin Khaleefa,
(It has been narrated) from Umar, son of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, from his father<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who repels from a group of Muslims, an adversity of water or fire, the Paradise would be Obligated for him’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Futr ibn Khalifah from ‘Amr ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn from his father (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘One who repulses a transgressor from Muslim’s (waters) or fire, will as a matter of necessity go to paradise.’”
